thread:
Leah: FYI we saw a burst of tenant churn at 08:02 PT in us-west2 where NIC tx queues spiked and a bunch of tenants hit hard token backpressure. This correlated with warm pool coldstarts + a big multi-request job.
Sam: Any particular tenant pattern? seq length, model type?
Leah: Mixed but mostly long-seq generative jobs on a few mid-tier tenants that suddenly ramped. The scheduler gave them short-lived shared-burst leases, but the NIC shaping penalized the hosts and others slowed down.
Diego: We need a better short-term isolation primitive than 'free-for-all shared burst'. Maybe a per-tenant burst-ledger with decay and local NIC budget reservation.
Anita: I like ledger idea. Operational constraints: the ledger should be forgiven quickly (seconds) so we don't break PLG UX, but also bounded to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
Sam: Proposal: implement a fractional burst ledger per tenant per AZ. Each ledger has tokens that refill on a sliding window. When ledger empty, router shifts to quantized variant or small worker within region. Only if region exhausted, can we allow cross-region with explicit egress tagging.
Leah: Also track host-level nic_usage and deprioritize tenants that exceed host_budget to prefer migrating their burst to a different host. Avoid host NIC queue overcommit.
Diego: Pseudo-config for the ledger prototype: 

```
burst_ledger:
  window_seconds: 60
  max_tokens_per_window: 1000   # ~tokens-per-minute per tenant
  refill_rate_pps: 16           # tokens per second approximation
  decay_half_life_seconds: 30  # how quickly borrowed tokens dissipate
  allow_host_migration: true
  migrate_if_host_nic_usage_pct_gt: 75

regional_fallback_order:
  - local_dedicated
  - local_burst_ledger
  - local_quantized
  - local_shared_short_live
  - cross_region (tagged)
```

Anita: We must add billing tags for "burst_ledger_used" and "migrated_for_nic". Cost team needs this to compute egress/compute deltas.
Sam: Alerting: add a KPI alert when host_nic_queue_ms > 100ms and burst_ledger_migrations > 10/min. Also add top-10 tenants by ledger drain rate.
Diego: For enterprise tenants, ledger caps should be configurable (some can opt-out of bursting). Default for enterprise: burst disabled unless SLA allow-burst=true.
Leah: Implementation concerns: we need atomic increment/decrement for ledger tokens across replicas. Suggest using local in-memory counters with occasional durable checkpoints to avoid cross-host contention. Worst-case we'll conservatively reject burst when unsure.
Anita: UX: add a warning header to API responses when burst_ledger applied: X-Redwood-Burst: used=120/1000 window=60s. That will help customers detect they're consuming bursts.
Sam: Can we run a 24-hour simulation using last month's traffic to tune max_tokens_per_window? I'll queue that.
Leah: Canary plan: roll ledger read-only mode in canary region (us-west2-canary) for 2 hours to collect metrics, then enable enforcement at 2% traffic for non-enterprise tenants, 6h ramp. infra-bot can schedule.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled -> router-service.ledger-canary at 2024-11-07T15:00:00Z (initiated by Sam).
Diego: I'll prepare dashboard panels: ledger_fill_level, ledger_consumed_per_min, host_nic_usage, cross_region_egress_tagged.
Anita: Cost note: if we avoid cross-region spills by using ledger+migration, we should see net egress drop; but compute might rise slightly due to migrations. Carlos will want an ROI number.
Leah: Great. Sam, please post simulation results and migration overhead estimate. I'll open the PR for the router changes and the runbook entry: "Burst ledger: read-only -> enforced canary -> full rollout; emergency rollback if host_nic_queue_ms > 150ms or cross-region tags spike."
Sam: Ack. Starting the simulation now. Will update in this thread. :rocket:
